design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (tool_rental_servicing). Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[6,6,6]; downtime credit (root) 6, ProBuild discount 6, engine overtime 6. Draw for task 1: prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[5,4,6,4].

WHY A GOOD TEST. A contractor asks only for credit for the days a towable boom lift sat broken on his site. The charter's downtime credit rule says the credit is fixed only after the agreement carries the ProBuild discount entry owed on its rental time and is not worked out until the agreement carries the engine overtime charge owed for its hour meter reading. Neither line stands at the opening, so the agent must read two prerequisite sentences, find in the ledger that the states do not hold, find in the other rules which write brings each state about, compute those two charges first (6 factors each) and only then compute the credit (6 factors) on the world those writes create. The difficulty is in discovering the tree and getting 18 factors right over reconciled history (time lines, meter, requests, inspection, ProBuild activity, Pro Credit ledger), never in picking a tool.

SCOPE. Claims rental_ext_probuild_rental_discount (post_probuild_rental_discount_391bfaed, agent), rental_ext_engine_overtime_charge (bill_engine_overtime_13bb4269, agent), rental_ext_downtime_credit (accept_downtime_credit_2dc14db7, user). Left for task 1: the damage-dispute cluster (deductible, missing accessories, refuelling, protected damage adjustment) on a consumer agreement - a disjoint tree of four problems on other events (fee lines of other fee types and rental_charge_adjusted), with its own user write. No policy or tool is shared.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root rental_ext_downtime_credit. Edge 1 -> rental_ext_probuild_rental_discount, kind value_input, gate disc_posted, form state, sentence "The downtime credit is fixed only after the agreement carries the ProBuild rental discount entry owed on its rental time." (affirmative). Edge 2 -> rental_ext_engine_overtime_charge, value_input, gate ot_posted, form state, sentence "The downtime credit is not worked out until the agreement carries the engine overtime charge owed for its hour meter reading at return." (negated). Four-point test: each joins this policy's result (the credit) to a record-visible line with an ordering connective (only after / not until), names no tool, id or code token, and is as strong as the condition (the entry owed, which is vacuous for a non-member or an unmetered unit). Exactly one write of the difficulty books a ProBuild discount line (the discount rule's) and exactly one books an overtime_hours fee line (the overtime rule's), so each state singles out one action. Derivation: sentence -> ledger shows only rental_time_charged x2 and rental_inspection_recorded -> the ProBuild rule says the discount is "posted once per agreement as one ProBuild discount line" and the overtime rule says the charge is "billed once per agreement at return as one overtime line" -> those two writes. Seed evidence of falsity: no rental_pro_discount_applied and no overtime_hours line on agreement RA-0583-204716 while the Gold membership is active and the meter moved 2214.3 -> 2332.9. Topological order: discount, overtime (parallel, commute), credit. Deletion sensitivity (executed with _author/calc.py): skipping the discount gives a credit of 1,681.37, skipping the overtime 1,157.04, against 1,491.69. user_scenario names neither problem; tools validate nothing.

FACTOR CARD (all from the executed sensitivity run on the handling-time world).
Discount (expected 298.60, all-baseline 212.00): pro_credit_standing_points - trade account active, 0 returned payments in 12 months (the 2025-07-01 NSF return is the near-miss, 15 months old) -> +1, baseline 277.40; membership_tenure_points - enrolled 2016-08-22, 120 months before checkout -> +1, baseline 277.40; late_return_points - returned the day after due-back -> -0.5, baseline 309.20; rental_spend_points - pro_activity tool_rental postings in 12 months 5,620.00 (the 2025-09-30 1,180.00 posting is the near-miss at 12 months; in_store and pro_desk spend excluded) -> +0.5, baseline 288.00; booking_ahead_points - reserved 10 days ahead -> +0.5, baseline 288.00; long_rental_bands (method) - weekly periods -> marginal bands, baseline flat 265.00.
Overtime (expected 526.79, all-baseline 0.00): shift_allowance_convention (method) - weekly periods -> 2x40+8 = 88 h, baseline 120 h gives 0.00; pro_credit_volume_hours - 5 tool rental invoices in 12 months (2024-09-04 invoice and the in_store invoices are near-misses) -> 8 h, baseline 753.36; malfunction_diagnostic_hours - 2 reports + confirmed -> 4 h, baseline 640.07; account_overtime_percentage - Pro Credit active + Gold -> 9%, baseline 12.5% gives 731.65; late_return_multiplier - 1 day late -> x1.25, baseline 421.43; rental_spend_multiplier - 5,620.00 -> x0.95, baseline 554.51.
Credit (expected 1,491.69, all-baseline 1,095.82): lost_day_counting (method) - collected unit returned after due-back -> report to due-back 6 days, baseline 7 days gives 1,690.58; account_goodwill_days - Pro Credit active + Gold -> +1 day, baseline 1,292.80; long_outage_days - 3x7 >= 15 -> +0.5 day, baseline 1,392.24; repeat_failure_multiplier - 2 reports -> x1.10, baseline 1,356.08; probuild_rental_activity_multiplier - 5 postings -> x1.10, baseline 1,356.08; pro_credit_rental_volume_multiplier - 5 invoices -> x1.05, baseline 1,420.65.
Multi-source: pro_credit_standing_points, malfunction_diagnostic_hours, account_overtime_percentage, account_goodwill_days. Cross-difficulty: trade (pro_credit_standing_points, pro_credit_volume_hours, account_overtime_percentage, account_goodwill_days, pro_credit_rental_volume_multiplier) and pro (rental_spend_points, rental_spend_multiplier, probuild_rental_activity_multiplier). No stamp decides a tier.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Discount write (rental_pro_discount_applied): rental_agg_pro_relationship and rental_pro_discount, no structured gates; membership active on the checkout date (enrolled 2016-08-22, active), class earns the discount (pro_discount_eligible true), no weekend-special time. Overtime write (rental_fee_charged): rental_reservations, rental_damage_protection, rental_return_fees, rental_delivery, rental_overdue_and_conversion, no structured gates; return fees are billed on returned, inspected equipment. Credit write (rental_malfunction_credit_issued): rental_malfunction gates malfunction_confirmed (inspection row outcome malfunction_confirmed on this agreement) and one_credit_per_report (no credit line carries the 2026-09-22 report; damage_cause not_applicable, so no misuse). No time gate applies to these three writes. Overwrites declared: rental_pro_discount and rental_agg_pro_relationship (flat tier % replaced by the agreement's discount rate with points and bands), rental_return_fees (overtime method), rental_malfunction (full-credit-within-hours / same-rates sentence replaced by lost days x net daily rental cost); every other base sentence stays in force.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Object: agreement RA-0583-204716 (single agreement of the renter). Rows aggregated: its two rental_time_charged lines, its inspection, its two malfunction reports. Credit booked against the most recent report (2026-09-22 14:10), not the 2026-09-18 report that was completed on site. Cross rows read only: one pro membership with 8 spend postings, one trade account with invoices, payments and one returned payment.

SEED ROWS. customers (identity), rental_agreements (dates, meter, rate, flags), rental_charges (2 time lines - base of every computation; inspection - eligibility and diagnostic tier), rental_requests (2 reports - anchor, repeat tier, report count), pro_memberships (tier, enrolment), pro_activity (spend and count tiers, near-miss posting), trade_accounts (status), trade_transactions (invoice count, returned-payment window, near-misses). Deleting any tier's evidence moves that factor to its fall-through and changes the figure (see factor card). The agreement is unpaid (Net 30 Pro Credit settlement later) and carries no deposit (waived for active Pro Credit) and no damage protection (declined with a certificate of insurance), so no protection, deposit or refund obligation is ignited by the new lines; balance after the call 856.50.

PERSONA. A terse contractor who raises only the dead days; identity (phone, EIN last four, ZIP), agreement number and 'towed both ways' given only on request; passive agreement to whatever entries the records require first; accepts the credit himself when handed the step and ends the call on hearing it is on the agreement. No figure, policy or prerequisite is in his text.

STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers(4695550417) -> verify(phone, 7316) -> read agreements, charges, requests, ProBuild membership and activity, Pro Credit account and ledger -> post discount 298.60 -> bill overtime 526.79 -> unlock and hand over the acceptance -> renter accepts 1,491.69 against the 2026-09-22 report. Verification: _author/calc.py replays gold with the real tools and evaluates each policy's compute on the world just before its step; check_compute --task 0 recomputes 298.6 / 526.79 / 1491.69 and every factor_sensitivity and baseline_result (COMPUTE OK).

DRAFT FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. Reading only the rules as prose, the tool schemas and the records: the credit rule's two sentences point at a discount line and an overtime line; the ledger lacks both; the discount rule (Gold 10% + 1 + 1 - 0.5 + 0.5 + 0.5 = 12.5%, weekly bands) gives 298.60; the overtime rule (118.6 - 88 - 8 - 4 = 18.6 h at 23.85, x1.25 x0.95) gives 526.79; the credit (7.5 days x 2,348.19/15 x1.10 x1.10 x1.05) gives 1,491.69 - same as gold.

REVISIONS. (1) check_extended flagged helper functions in task_tools.py as undiscoverable tools -> bodies inlined into each tool; re-run TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK. (2) replay flagged empty foreign-key fields as dangling -> empty id fields dropped from seed rows; inspection row given the 2026-09-22 report as its related request (needed as one_credit_per_report evidence); re-run REPLAY OK. (3) Credit first had 5 factors against a draw of 6 -> added pro_credit_rental_volume_multiplier; recomputed 1,491.69.

REVISIONS round 2 (policy-task audit audits/policy_task/tool_rental_servicing/). F-A1 (compute zeroed every point when the tier percentage was 0) -> rate_pct is now MX(0, tier% + points) for any membership active on the checkout date, result gated on that eligibility only; rule now says the tier percentage counts 'a percentage of zero included', points change the rate 'whatever the tier's own percentage, and the rate never goes below zero'. Probe on this world with the tier set to ProBuild Bronze (0%): rate 2.5%, discount 86.60 under both rule and compute. F-A2 (compute read the current status) -> rule now defines from the record: 'A membership counts as active on the checkout date when it was enrolled on or before the checkout date and its record shows it active, or shows it suspended or closed with the suspension or closing dated after the checkout date; a membership whose record shows it pending verification, or suspended or closed on or before the checkout date, does not count.' and member_ok implements exactly that (probes: suspended 2026-10-01 -> 298.60; suspended 2026-09-01 -> 0; closed 2026-09-10 -> 0; no membership -> 0). The tier sentence now names the tier 'the membership's record shows on the day the discount is posted' (the override-declarations note on 'holds'). T0-O1 -> the 2025-07-01 NSF return now carries its Net 30 returned payment fee of 35.00 (trade_fee_assessed, returned_payment_fee, referencing the returned line), and the 2025-07-05 wire covers invoice plus fee (2,245.40); no factor reads trade fees. O-6 -> tool receipts say 'resulting balance'. This world is unchanged: 298.60 / 526.79 / 1,491.69, COMPUTE OK.

REVISIONS round 3 (re-audit revision_2). Task 0 passed with no new item. R2-O1 (a membership suspended on the checkout date and reinstated since reads as active under the record-based definition) is an observation: the pro schema keeps no reinstatement history and suspended_date is empty unless suspended, so no seedable world separates the two readings; nothing changed in this task. N-1, R2-O2 and R2-O3 concern task 1's policies (see 1.json). Figures unchanged: 298.60 / 526.79 / 1,491.69.
user_scenario:
You are Rafael Quintanilla Brandt, owner of Quintanilla Steel Erectors LLC in Dallas, calling Ridgeline Customer Care from a job trailer on a Thursday morning. You talk like a busy contractor: short, direct, a little dry, never rude. Three weeks ago your crew rented a towable boom lift from the Ridgeline rental center, store 0583, and towed it to a medical-office job. The lift kept faulting out; you called it in, the store had someone look at it, and after it died again you reported it a second time, and it sat unusable on your site until your crew towed it back. You are calling for one thing: I want the days that lift sat dead on my site taken off the bill. You open with that, in your own words, and you do not list any other charges or programs.

You do not know internal reference numbers. When the agent asks how to find you, you give your phone number, 4695550417. If asked to confirm your identity, you give the last four of the business EIN, 7316, and, only if a further detail is requested, the billing ZIP code 75229; your email, if asked, is rafael.brandt@quintanillasteel.com and your date of birth is 1979-03-14. If the agent asks which rental, you read the agreement number off your paperwork: RA-0583-204716, the 35-foot towable boom lift. You do not remember the exact dates or hours off-hand and say the store's records will have them. If asked whether the lift was delivered, you say no, your crew towed it both ways. If asked about other Ridgeline accounts or memberships, you say the business has the usual ones and the agent can see them on file; you do not recite numbers.

You do not know how Ridgeline works out a credit and you do not suggest any amount. If the agent explains that other entries have to be put on the agreement before the credit can be figured, you say something like "fine, go ahead and put through whatever the records say has to be on there first" and let the agent do it; you do not ask what they are or argue about them. If the agent says a charge is going on the bill, you accept it without comment as long as the agent is the one handling it. When the agent tells you the credit amount and hands you the step to accept it, you will accept it yourself, using exactly the agreement, report and amount the agent gives you, and you then tell the agent what the confirmation shows. If the agent instead offers to book the credit for you without your acceptance, you say you would rather accept it yourself, as the agent offered the remedy to you. Once you hear the credit is on the agreement, you thank the agent and end the call; you do not ask for anything else.

edges.condition: For a renter whose ProBuild membership was active on the checkout date, the agreement's ledger carries the ProBuild rental discount line computed under the ProBuild rental discount rule.
edges.policy_source: The downtime credit is fixed only after the agreement carries the ProBuild rental discount entry owed on its rental time.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The renter's Gold membership was active on the 2026-09-14 checkout date and Aerial and Lifting earns the discount, so a ProBuild discount entry is owed on the rental time, yet the agreement's ledger holds only the two rental time lines and the inspection: no discount line stands.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 10 books a rental_pro_discount_applied line of 298.60 on the agreement; disc_posted becomes 298.60 and the net daily rental cost falls from 176.453 to 156.546 (with the overtime posted).

edges.condition: For metered equipment, the agreement's ledger carries the engine overtime line computed under the engine overtime rule from the hour meter readings at checkout and return.
edges.policy_source: The downtime credit is not worked out until the agreement carries the engine overtime charge owed for its hour meter reading at return.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The unit is metered (8 engine hours per billed day) and its meter moved 118.6 hours, so an engine overtime charge is owed for the reading at return, yet no overtime fee line stands on the agreement.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 12 books a rental_fee_charged line with fee_type overtime_hours of 526.79; ot_posted becomes 526.79 and the net daily rental cost rises from 121.427 to 156.546 (with the discount posted).

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisites are parallel: the ProBuild discount reads only rental time lines, membership, Pro Credit and dates, and the overtime charge reads only the meter, time lines, requests, inspection and the other accounts; neither reads the other's line. Replaying the gold with steps 10-11 and 11-12 swapped gives the same discount (298.60), the same overtime (526.79), the same credit (1,491.69) and the same terminal hash, since every row id is a content hash of its own arguments. The credit itself comes last because both sentences of its rule wait on the two lines.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 10 leaves disc_posted at 0.00; the credit recomputes to 1,681.37 instead of 1,491.69 and the discount line is missing from the terminal ledger.
Skipping step 12 leaves ot_posted at 0.00; the credit recomputes to 1,157.04 instead of 1,491.69 and the overtime line is missing from the terminal ledger.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona speaks only of the breakdown and the downtime credit. It never mentions a ProBuild discount, ProBuild membership, Pro Credit, engine hours, meter readings or overtime, and contains no hint that something must be settled first; its only lines about other items are passive: if the agent says other entries must go on first, he agrees to whatever the records require.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: accept_downtime_credit_2dc14db7 in task_tools.py reads the agreement only to copy customer_id, agreement_number and balance_due, creates the credit line and updates balance_due; it never looks for a discount or overtime line and never returns an error, so a credit accepted before steps 10 and 12 would be written at whatever amount is passed.
